clue.text: Rise includes unemployment benefit for a youngster

indicators.note: one word includes another when it holds that second word within it, here the rise around the benefit

parts.note: a rise is an ascent, a climb upwards
the dole is the informal British name for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A rise in benefit payments is arranged for a young person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' looks like a verb in the surface but is a noun, the climb, which wraps around the benefit; 'for a' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager not yet adult is a youngster.

indicators.note: the king letter goes in, placed within the word for appropriate
the word for appropriate is the setting that the king letter is mounted in, like a jewel

parts.note: what is appropriate or fitting is due
K is the standard abbreviation for king, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A nobleman is pictured as a king in a fitting setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British peerage, a nobleman.

clue.text: Pound is good in France and capital elsewhere

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
taken as written
bon is the French word for good

explanation.surface: A note on currency: the pound is good in France and capital somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elsewhere' qualifies the capital: not France but Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital city of Portugal, a country other than France.

parts.note: a boxing blow from a burly fighter, read instead as a superior cut of beef from the butcher

explanation.surface: A hefty boxer throws a powerful uppercut.
explanation.definitionFit: The loin's upper part gives a prime joint of beef, so it is a top-quality cut of meat.

clue.text: See a letter goes to the agent

parts.note: E is one letter of the alphabet
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Someone observes a letter being passed to a secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, to see.

parts.note: a cruel, harsh government by one despot, stated almost plainly

explanation.definitionFit: Despotic government that crushes its subjects is the classic sense of this word.

clue.text: Nepal organised equipment for mountain staff

indicators.note: organised means put in a new order, so the letters of Nepal are rearranged

parts.note: stock is the equipment or supplies kept on hand

explanation.surface: Equipment for a Himalayan trek has been organised in Nepal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' makes ALPEN from NEPAL; 'for' links. 'staff' looks like the climbing team but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron-pointed walking pole used by climbers is a staff for mountains.

parts.note: seems to mean a space engineer, but Rocket was the famous early steam locomotive of 1829

explanation.definitionFit: George and Robert Stephenson built the locomotive Rocket, winner of the Rainhill trials.

parts.note: a small amount of ink, read as ink dropped on paper, making a stain

explanation.definitionFit: A stain or smudge left by spilled ink on a page is the thing meant.

clue.text: Big build-up in New York, for example

definitions.text: Big build-up in New York, for example

parts.words: Big build-up in New York, for example
parts.note: sounds like a traffic jam or hype, but means a tall building built up in Manhattan

explanation.surface: Congestion builds up badly in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A very tall building, typical of Manhattan, is a big structure built upwards.

clue.text: Napping, the general is swallowed by a snake

indicators.note: one thing swallowed by another ends up inside it, so the general goes inside the snake

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A dozing general gets swallowed whole by a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone napping is sleeping, dozing off.

clue.text: It may be a bit off the mark

definitions.text: It may be a bit off the mark

parts.words: It may be a bit off the mark
parts.note: sounds like a slight miss, but means a small coin worth a fraction of the German mark

explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth of the old German mark was this small coin, a bit of that currency.

parts.note: a churchwarden is also a long clay tobacco pipe, so the fancies are dreams nursed by pipe smokers

explanation.definitionFit: Unrealistic hopes or fantasies, from opium-smokers' visions, are such fancies.

parts.note: seems to be about a bank, but means overstate a story, drawing it bigger than life

explanation.definitionFit: To overstate or embellish a report is to describe it beyond the truth.

parts.note: GI is a US soldier
an ant is an insect, with six feet

explanation.surface: A huge soldier stands fully six feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six footer' looks like a tall man's height, but it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gigantic or colossal is enormous.

clue.text: Mother's possibly seen going round in the altogether

indicators.note: one piece going round another surrounds it, so the jumbled letters enclose the mother piece
possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters of the word seen

parts.note: MA is mother, with the possessive adding S

explanation.surface: Mother has perhaps been spotted wandering around naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns SEEN into ENSE. 'in the altogether' suggests nudity, but here means all together, as a whole group.
explanation.definitionFit: Done all as one group, collectively, is the sense of this French phrase.

clue.text: There's a moral in the thickness of thieves

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: Even close-knit criminals have a moral code of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'thick as thieves', meaning very close.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral principle or code of conduct is an ethic.

clue.text: Stylish outfit seen in New York

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are seen in the city's abbreviation, placed inside it

parts.note: outfit splits as 'out fit': the word fit put out of order gives these letters

explanation.surface: A fashionable outfit is spotted on the streets of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue word 'outfit' does double duty by splitting: 'out' is an anagram signal on 'fit', making IFT. It looks like clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neat, smart and skilful in style is described as nifty.

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a dog is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a peke is a Pekinese, a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: Someone points to the top dog, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: The summit or highest point of something is its top.

parts.note: the cheapest seats in the highest gallery, nearest heaven and its deities

explanation.definitionFit: The upper gallery of a theatre is traditionally named after heavenly deities, being nearest the sky.

clue.text: Orphan who may get a gun

definitions.meaning: Little Orphan ... is the famous American comic-strip orphan
refers to the musical ... Get Your Gun about sharpshooter ... Oakley

explanation.definitionFit: Both a famous cartoon orphan and the musical's sharpshooting heroine bear this girl's name.

definitions.meaning: rising from bed or standing up
a rebellion, an uprising, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Getting out of bed is rising, and an uprising or rebellion is a rising.

parts.note: seems to mean succeeding in a career, but means growing old

explanation.definitionFit: People advanced in years are said to be getting on, old.

parts.note: sounds like a food truck, but a chow is a breed of dog and this cart carries dogs

explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled carriage, originally with a box for sporting dogs, is a cart for dogs.

parts.note: sounds like arriving punctually, but means recording arrival time at work on a time clock

explanation.definitionFit: Workers register arrival at work by stamping a card on a time recorder.

definitions.meaning: one of Titania's fairy attendants in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
what spiders spin in the corners of rooms

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare named a fairy after the spider's silken net, often found in corners of rooms.

definitions.meaning: The Comedy of ... is the Shakespeare play about two pairs of twins

explanation.definitionFit: Blunders are mistakes, and the word also completes the title of Shakespeare's comedy of twins.

clue.text: Request to remain true to type?

definitions.text: Request to remain true to type?

parts.words: Request to remain true to type?
parts.note: sounds like a plea for consistency, but is a proofreader's mark asking that crossed-out type be kept

explanation.definitionFit: A proof-correction instruction, Latin for 'let it stand', tells the printer to keep the original text.

parts.note: singularly hints at the number one: a single knockout punch

explanation.definitionFit: A single heavy punch, one that settles it, is British slang for a knockout blow.

clue.text: Wire netting not good, somehow twist together

indicators.note: somehow signals the remaining letters are rearranged in some new way
not means the letter for good is left out of the fodder

explanation.surface: Wire netting of poor quality is somehow twisted together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' removes G from NETTING, leaving NETTIN, and 'somehow' rearranges WIRE plus NETTIN into the ten-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlace or entwine strands is to twist them together.

clue.text: Successful conclusion to a board meeting

definitions.text: Successful conclusion to a board meeting

parts.words: Successful conclusion to a board meeting
parts.note: sounds like company directors, but the board is a chessboard and the conclusion is ...

explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate, often shortened, ends a chess game in victory.

parts.note: sounds like a street location, but means Lincoln's celebrated 1863 speech

explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln delivered his celebrated speech at this Pennsylvania battlefield town in 1863.
